source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with massive bleeding from a stab wound is in which type of shock?
questions.rationale: Hypovolemic shock results from loss of blood or plasma.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hypovolemic Shock (PDF p. 319)
questions.quote: Hemorrhage/Excessive bleeding

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Shock after a massive anterior-wall MI is classified as:
questions.rationale: Cardiogenic shock is pump failure from MI, HF, or tamponade.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cardiogenic Shock (PDF p. 319)
questions.quote: Myocardial infarction

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with a cervical spinal cord injury has hypotension with bradycardia and warm, dry skin. This suggests:
questions.rationale: Loss of sympathetic tone below the lesion causes vasodilation and bradycardia.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Neurogenic Shock (PDF p. 319)
questions.quote: loss of autonomic nervous system function below the level of the lesion

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client develops wheezing and hypotension minutes after IV antibiotic starts. After stopping the drug, the nurse gives:
questions.rationale: Remove the antigen and give epinephrine for vasoconstriction and bronchodilation; diphenhydramine follows.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Anaphylactic Shock (PDF p. 319)
questions.quote: Epinephrine is given for its vasoconstrictive action (emergency drug).

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Septic shock is most commonly caused by:
questions.rationale: Septic shock is the body's reaction to bacterial toxins, generally gram-negative.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Septic Shock (PDF p. 319)
questions.quote: generally gram-negative infection

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Hypertension caused by pheochromocytoma is classified as:
questions.rationale: Secondary HTN has an identifiable cause: renal disease, pheochromocytoma, Cushing's, coarctation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Secondary Hypertension (PDF p. 320)
questions.quote: Pheochromocytoma

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which lifestyle factor increases the risk for essential hypertension?
questions.rationale: Risks: high salt, caffeine, alcohol, smoking, inactivity, low potassium, calcium, magnesium.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Essential Hypertension (PDF p. 320)
questions.quote: High salt intake or caffeine

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: ACE inhibitors such as captopril lower blood pressure by:
questions.rationale: ACE inhibitors reduce peripheral resistance and aldosterone without reflex tachycardia.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, ACE Inhibitors (PDF p. 320)
questions.quote: Decrease secretion of aldosterone

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which diuretic is potassium-sparing?
questions.rationale: Spironolactone spares potassium; loops and thiazides waste it.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Diuretics (PDF p. 321)
questions.quote: Spironolactone (Aldactone)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A 28-year-old heavy smoker has instep claudication and rubor with absent pedal pulses. This suggests:
questions.rationale: Thromboangiitis obliterans affects young male smokers with claudication and rubor.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Buerger's Disease (PDF p. 321)
questions.quote: Heavy smoking and chewing tobacco

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the most important teaching for a client with Buerger's disease?
questions.rationale: Smoking cessation halts progression.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Buerger's Disease (PDF p. 321)
questions.quote: Heavy smoking and chewing tobacco

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Raynaud's phenomenon shows which color sequence in the fingers?
questions.rationale: Vasospasm causes pallor (white), cyanosis (blue), then reactive hyperemia (red).
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Raynaud's Phenomenon (PDF p. 321)
questions.quote: The characteristic sequence of color change of Raynaud's phenomenon is described as white, blue, and red.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which advice helps a client with Raynaud's phenomenon who works in an air-conditioned office?
questions.rationale: Avoid cold and nicotine; keep warm clothing available.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Raynaud's Nursing Care (PDF p. 322)
questions.quote: Sweater should be available when entering air-conditioned rooms

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Virchow's triad of DVT risk includes vessel injury, altered coagulation, and:
questions.rationale: Virchow's triad: vessel wall injury, venous stasis, hypercoagulability.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Venous Thromboembolism (PDF p. 322)
questions.quote: Venous stasis (stasis of blood)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which measure prevents DVT in a postoperative client?
questions.rationale: Compression stockings, SC heparin or LMWH, and early ambulation prevent DVT.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, DVT Prevention (PDF p. 322)
questions.quote: Preventive measures include the application of graduated compression stockings

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which laboratory value is monitored for a client on warfarin?
questions.rationale: Monitor PT/INR for warfarin and aPTT for heparin.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, DVT Nursing Management (PDF p. 322)
questions.quote: the nurse must frequently monitor the aPTT, prothrombin time, and INR

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: When should an ambulatory client apply graduated compression stockings?
questions.rationale: Remove at night and reapply before legs are lowered to the floor in the morning.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Alert (PDF p. 322)
questions.quote: reapplied before the legs are lowered from the bed to the floor in the morning

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A spindle-shaped aneurysm involving the entire circumference of an artery is:
questions.rationale: Fusiform is symmetric; saccular is one-sided; dissecting splits layers; false is a pulsating hematoma.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Aneurysm Types (PDF p. 323)
questions.quote: Fusiform aneurysm—symmetric, spindle shaped expansion

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The respiratory center in the medulla mainly responds to blood levels of:
questions.rationale: The medulla responds to CO2; carotid and aortic chemoreceptors respond to hypoxemia.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Respiratory Anatomy (PDF p. 324)
questions.quote: The respiratory center in the medulla is sensitive to concentration of carbon dioxide in the blood.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the basic gas-exchange unit of the lungs?
questions.rationale: O2 and CO2 diffuse across the alveolar-capillary membrane.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Respiratory Anatomy (PDF p. 324)
questions.quote: Basic gas-exchange unit of the respiratory system is the alveoli.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Before using a corticosteroid nasal spray for allergic rhinitis, the client should:
questions.rationale: Blow the nose before applying medication for maximal relief.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Allergic Rhinitis (PDF p. 325)
questions.quote: the patient is instructed to blow the nose before applying any medication into the nasal cavity

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The common cold is highly contagious because the virus is shed:
questions.rationale: Virus is shed about 2 days before symptoms and during the early symptomatic phase.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Viral Rhinitis (PDF p. 325)
questions.quote: virus is shed for about 2 days before the symptoms appear

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the drug of choice for bacterial (streptococcal) pharyngitis?
questions.rationale: Penicillin is the treatment of choice; cephalosporins and macrolides are alternatives.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Acute Pharyngitis (PDF p. 325)
questions.quote: Penicillin is the treatment of choice

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which comfort measure helps a client with acute pharyngitis?
questions.rationale: Warm saline gargles, cool drinks, popsicles, soft diet, and ice collar soothe the throat.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Acute Pharyngitis (PDF p. 325)
questions.quote: Warm saline gargles or throat irrigations
